en.title: The simple future
en.summary: English forms the future with will and the base form.

paragraphs: English has no future ending on the verb. Instead, the future is formed with the modal verb will and the base form of the main verb. Will is used for predictions, spontaneous decisions, promises and offers.

blocks.html:
FormExample
statementI will go. She will go.
questionWill you go?
negativeI will not (won't) go.
short formI'll, you'll, she'll, we'll, they'll

paragraphs: Will is the same for every person. The main verb always stays in the base form: She will go, not She will goes. In formal British English shall is sometimes used with I and we, especially in questions: Shall I open the window?

blocks.html:
UseExample
predictionIt will be sunny tomorrow.
spontaneous decisionThe phone is ringing. I'll answer it.
promiseI will call you tonight.
offerI'll carry your bag.
refusal (won't)The car won't start.
fact about the futureThe meeting will start at nine.

items: **probably**: She will probably come. (the adverb goes after will)
**I think**, **I expect**, **I hope**: I think it will rain.
**tomorrow, next week, soon, in two days**
Wrong: **I will to go.** Right: **I will go.**
Wrong: **She will goes.** Right: **She will go.**
Wrong: **If it will rain, we'll stay.** Right: **If it rains, we'll stay.** (no will in the if-clause)

ro.title: Viitorul simplu
ro.summary: Viitorul simplu exprimă o acțiune viitoare și se formează dintr-un verb auxiliar urmat de infinitiv.

paragraphs: Viitorul simplu arată acțiuni care se vor petrece mai târziu. Folosim acest timp pentru planuri, promisiuni sau predicții. Este forma standard și literară a viitorului în limba română.

Formăm viitorul simplu cu formele specifice ale verbului auxiliar „a vrea”. După auxiliar adăugăm infinitivul scurt al verbului, adică fără particula „a”. Auxiliarul își schimbă forma după persoană, dar verbul principal rămâne neschimbat.
